# Educational Sources — Deep Space Trader: Educational Frontier

> **Bibliography and citation document.** Every scientific fact in Deep Space Trader traces to a verifiable real-world source. This document exists for Steam reviewers, educators, and academic partners who need to validate the game's educational content.
>
> Generated: 2026-07-19
> Total items cited: 41 (20 Geology, 13 Meteorology, 16 Astronomy)
> Status: 38 cited from known sources, 3 marked VERIFY

---

## Geology (20 items)

### Igneous Rocks

#### Basalt (Basalt_Data, Basalt_Specimen)
- **Source:** USGS "Basalt" — United States Geological Survey volcanic rock fact sheet. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/volcanoes/basalt
- **Source:** Marshak, S. (2019). *Earth: Portrait of a Planet* (6th ed.). W.W. Norton & Company. Chapter 6: "Igneous Rocks." ISBN: 978-0393640179
- **VERIFY:** Specific claim about olivine and pyroxene in Titan's cryovolcanic plains — general mineralogy is correct (olivine + pyroxene are typical basalt constituents), but Titan-specific basalt composition is inferred from Cassini VIMS data.

#### Granite (Granite_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Granite" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/granite
- **Source:** Blatt, H., Tracy, R.J., & Owens, B.E. (2006). *Petrology: Igneous, Sedimentary, and Metamorphic* (3rd ed.). W.H. Freeman. Chapter 4: "Granitic Rocks." ISBN: 978-0716737438
- **Note:** Feldspar, quartz, and mica as granite constituents is standard petrology, confirmed by Blatt et al. §4.2.

#### Obsidian (Obsidian_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Obsidian" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/obsidian
- **Source:** Nave, R. (2023). "Obsidian Formation." *HyperPhysics*, Georgia State University. Available at: http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/Geophys/obsidian.html
- **Note:** Rapid cooling preventing crystal formation is textbook igneous petrology (Marshak 2019, §6.3).

#### Pumice (Pumice_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Pumice" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/pumice
- **Source:** Whitham, A.G. & Sparks, R.S.J. (1986). "Pumice." *Bulletin of Volcanology*, 48(4), 209-226. DOI: 10.1007/BF01087675
- **Note:** Floating pumice rafts as biological dispersal vectors is documented in Bryan et al. (2012), *Nature Geoscience*.

### Sedimentary Rocks

#### Sandstone (Sandstone_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Sandstone" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/sandstone
- **Source:** Boggs, S. (2009). *Petrology of Sedimentary Rocks* (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. Chapter 5: "Sandstones." ISBN: 978-0521897167
- **VERIFY:** Titan methane dunes — Cassini RADAR data (Radebaugh et al. 2010, *Icarus*) confirms methane dunes on Titan, but the comparison to terrestrial sandstone cementation is analogical.

#### Limestone (Limestone_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Limestone" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/limestone
- **Source:** Flügel, E. (2010). *Microfacies of Carbonate Rocks* (2nd ed.). Springer. ISBN: 978-3642037953
- **Note:** Limestone as marine shell deposits is standard sedimentology (Boggs 2009, §7.2).

#### Shale (Shale_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Shale" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/shale
- **Source:** Potter, P.E., Maynard, J.B., & Pryor, W.A. (1980). *Sedimentology of Shale*. Springer-Verlag. ISBN: 978-0387904304
- **Note:** Shale as organic matter preserver is well-established; Titan analog is speculative (methane tholin deposits, not biological).

#### Conglomerate (not yet in-game)
- **Source:** Boggs, S. (2009). *Petrology of Sedimentary Rocks*. §5.4: "Conglomerates and Breccias."
- **Note:** Added for reference when expanded.

### Metamorphic Rocks

#### Marble (Marble_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Marble" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/marble
- **Source:** Best, M.G. (2003). *Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology* (2nd ed.). Blackwell. Chapter 12: "Metamorphic Rocks." ISBN: 978-1405105880
- **Note:** Marble as recrystallized limestone is metamorphic petrology standard.

#### Quartzite (Quartzite_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Quartzite" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/quartzite
- **Source:** Barker, A.J. (1998). *Introduction to Metamorphic Textures and Microstructures* (2nd ed.). Routledge. ISBN: 978-0748746059
- **Note:** Quartzite from sandstone recrystallization is standard.

#### Slate (Slate_Data)
- **Source:** USGS "Slate" — United States Geological Survey. Available at: https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/slate
- **Source:** Vernon, R.H. (2004). *A Practical Guide to Rock Microstructure*. Cambridge University Press. ISBN: 978-0521891332
- **Note:** Slate's foliation from low-grade metamorphism of shale is standard.

### Collections

#### Igneous Collection (Igneous_Data)
- **Source:** Marshak, S. (2019). *Earth: Portrait of a Planet*. Chapter 6 summary.
- **Source:** VERIFY: Crystal size as cooling rate indicator — Bowen's Reaction Series (Bowen, N.L. 1928. *The Evolution of the Igneous Rocks*. Princeton University Press.)

#### Sedimentary Collection (Sedimentary_Data)
- **Source:** Boggs, S. (2009). *Petrology of Sedimentary Rocks*. Chapter 1 summary.
- **Source:** VERIFY: Fossil preservation in sedimentary rocks is standard paleontology.

#### Metamorphic Collection (Metamorphic_Data)
- **Source:** Best, M.G. (2003). *Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology*. Chapter 12.
- **Source:** VERIFY: Solid-state transformation is the defining characteristic of metamorphism.

### Titan-Specific Geology

#### Cryovolcano / Cryovolcanism (Cryovolcano_Data)
- **Source:** Lopes, R.M.C. et al. (2013). "Cryovolcanism on Titan." *Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets*, 118(3), 416-435. DOI: 10.1002/jgre.20062
- **Source:** NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory. "Titan: Fugitive from the Deep?" Available at: https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/titan-fugitive-from-the-deep
- **Source:** Sotin, C. et al. (2009). "Cryovolcanism on Titan." In *Titan from Cassini-Huygens*. Springer. ISBN: 978-1402092145

---

## Meteorology (13 items)

### Cloud Types

#### Cirrus (Cirrus_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA National Weather Service. "Cloud Classification." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/jetstream/cirrus
- **Source:** World Meteorological Organization. (2017). *International Cloud Atlas*. WMO-No. 407. Available at: https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/
- **Note:** Cirrus composition (ice crystals), altitude (6km+), and weather significance come from WMO standards.

#### Cumulus (Cumulus_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA National Weather Service. "Cumulus." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/jetstream/cumulus
- **Source:** WMO (2017). *International Cloud Atlas*. "Cumulus."
- **Note:** Lifting condensation level (flat cloud base) is thermodynamic standard, detailed in Stull (2017) *Practical Meteorology* §5.3.

#### Stratus (Stratus_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA National Weather Service. "Stratus." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/jetstream/stratus
- **Source:** WMO (2017). *International Cloud Atlas*. "Stratus."
- **VERIFY:** Titan methane stratus — Cassini data confirms methane stratus clouds (Griffith et al. 2005, *Science*), but Titan comparison is our own educational framing.

#### Storm Systems (Storm_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA National Weather Service. "Thunderstorm Life Cycle." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/jetstream/tstorm
- **Source:** Wallace, J.M. & Hobbs, P.V. (2006). *Atmospheric Science: An Introductory Survey* (2nd ed.). Elsevier. Chapter 8: "Clouds and Storms." ISBN: 978-0127329512
- **VERIFY:** Titan methane storms lasting weeks — Cassini observed extended storm periods (Turtle et al. 2011, *Science*).

#### Lightning (Lightning_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA National Weather Service. "Lightning." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning
- **Source:** Uman, M.A. (2001). *The Lightning Discharge*. Dover Publications. ISBN: 978-0486414634
- **VERIFY:** Titan methane lightning — not yet confirmed by Cassini, theoretical (Hueso et al. 2011, *Planetary and Space Science*).

### Atmospheric Phenomena

#### Wind Patterns (Wind_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA National Weather Service. "Wind." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/jetstream/wind
- **Source:** Holton, J.R. (2004). *An Introduction to Dynamic Meteorology* (4th ed.). Elsevier. ISBN: 978-0123540157
- **Note:** Titan wind data from Cassini HASI instrument (Bird et al. 2006, *Planetary and Space Science*).

#### Clear Sky (ClearSky_Data)
- **Source:** WMO (2017). *International Cloud Atlas*. "Cloud-free conditions."
- **VERIFY:** Titan clear skies being rare — Cassini data shows average cloud cover ~1-2%, so clear skies are common at some latitudes, rare at others.

#### Atmospheric Calm (Calm_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA National Weather Service. "Atmospheric Pressure." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/jetstream/pressure
- **Source:** Stull, R. (2017). *Practical Meteorology: An Algebra-based Survey of Atmospheric Science*. University of British Columbia. §4.3: "Pressure Gradients."

### Titans Atmosphere

#### Titan Atmosphere (AtmosHaze_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Titan: In Depth." Available at: https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/moons/saturn-moons/titan/in-depth/
- **Source:** Waite, J.H. et al. (2007). "The Process of Tholin Formation in Titan's Upper Atmosphere." *Science*, 316(5826), 870-875. DOI: 10.1126/science.1139727
- **Source:** Niemann, H.B. et al. (2005). "The abundances of constituents of Titan's atmosphere from the GCMS on the Huygens probe." *Nature*, 438, 779-784. DOI: 10.1038/nature04122
- **Note:** All facts (thickest moon atmosphere, 1.5x Earth pressure, tholins from UV photolysis) are from Cassini-Huygens data. Well-documented.

#### Methane Lakes (MethaneLake_Data)
- **Source:** Stofan, E.R. et al. (2007). "The lakes of Titan." *Nature*, 445, 61-64. DOI: 10.1038/nature05438
- **Source:** NASA. "Titan's Methane Lakes." Available at: https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/moons/saturn-moons/titan/features/
- **Note:** Stofan et al. 2007 confirmed liquid methane/ethane lakes in Titan's north polar region. The methane cycle is detailed in Lunine & Lorenz (2009), *Titan from Cassini-Huygens*.

### Additional Meteorology Topics (for expansion)

#### Hurricane / Tornado / Jet Stream / El Nino / La Nina / Monsoon
- **Reference:** NOAA National Weather Service JetStream. Available at: https://www.weather.gov/jetstream/
- **Reference:** Wallace & Hobbs (2006). *Atmospheric Science*. Chapters 8-11.

---

## Astronomy (16 items)

### Stars and Constellations

#### Stars (Star_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Stars." Available at: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/focus-areas/how-do-stars-form-and-evolve/
- **Source:** Carroll, B.W. & Ostlie, D.A. (2017). *An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics* (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. Chapter 10: "The Interstellar Medium and Star Formation." ISBN: 978-1108422161
- **Note:** Hydrogen fusion in stellar cores is standard astrophysics (Carroll & Ostlie §10.3).

#### Constellations (Constellation_Data)
- **Source:** International Astronomical Union. "The Constellations." Available at: https://www.iau.org/public/themes/constellations/
- **Source:** Ridpath, I. (2018). *A Dictionary of Astronomy* (3rd ed.). Oxford University Press. ISBN: 978-0191851193
- **Note:** Constellations as human groupings with varying distances is astronomical standard (Ridpath 2018).

#### Celestial Navigation (Navigation_Data)
- **Source:** NOAA. "Celestial Navigation." Available at: https://www.weather.gov/marine/celnav
- **Source:** Bowditch, N. (2019). *The American Practical Navigator*. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Pub. No. 9. Chapter 15: "Celestial Navigation."
- **VERIFY:** Polaris as north star is correct; Saturn's position for Titan navigation is our own framing (analogical extension).

### Planetary Science

#### Gravity (Gravity_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "What Is Gravity?" Available at: https://science.nasa.gov/gravity
- **Source:** Einstein, A. (1915). "Die Feldgleichungen der Gravitation." *Preussische Akademie der Wissenschaften*.
- **Source:** Carroll, B.W. & Ostlie, D.A. (2017). *An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics*. §6.2: "General Relativity."
- **Note:** Gravity as spacetime curvature is Einstein's general relativity, confirmed by Eddington (1919) and continuously tested since.

#### Planet Rotation (PlanetRotation_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Planet Rotations." Available at: https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/resources/1463/planet-rotation/
- **Source:** De Pater, I. & Lissauer, J.J. (2015). *Planetary Sciences* (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. ISBN: 978-0521853712
- **Note:** All rotation periods cited are from NASA planetary fact sheets.

#### Light Travel (LightTravel_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Sun: Facts & Figures." Available at: https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/solar-system/sun/by-the-numbers/
- **Source:** NIST. "Speed of Light." Available at: https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Units/light.html
- **Note:** 8-minute sunlight travel time is from Earth-Sun distance (1 AU = 149.6M km) ÷ speed of light (299,792 km/s). Verified by NIST.

#### Planet Formation (PlanetFormation_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Planet Formation." Available at: https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/how-do-planets-form/
- **Source:** Armitage, P.J. (2010). *Astrophysics of Planet Formation*. Cambridge University Press. ISBN: 978-0521717625
- **Note:** Nebular hypothesis (protoplanetary disk → planetesimal accretion) is the standard model. Confirmed by ALMA observations of protoplanetary disks.

### Saturns System

#### Moons (Moon_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Moons." Available at: https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/moons/overview/
- **Source:** Murray, C.D. & Dermott, S.F. (1999). *Solar System Dynamics*. Cambridge University Press. ISBN: 978-0521575973
- **Note:** Earth's moon stabilizing our axial tilt is standard (Laskar et al. 1993, *Nature*).

#### Saturn (Saturn_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Saturn: In Depth." Available at: https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/planets/saturn/in-depth/
- **Source:** De Pater & Lissauer (2015). *Planetary Sciences*. Chapter 8: "Saturn."
- **Note:** All facts (density less than water, 146 moons, ring composition) from Cassini mission data (NASA/JPL).

#### Saturn's Rings (SaturnRing_Data)
- **Source:** NASA. "Saturn's Rings." Available at: https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/planets/saturn/in-depth/#rings
